normalFinding.default: Alert and oriented to person, place, time and situation.

steps: Ask the patient their name.
Ask where they are and what the date is.
Ask why they are here today.

normalFinding.default: Smell intact to a familiar odour in each nostril.

steps: Only test when indicated.
Occlude one nostril and, with the eyes closed, ask the patient to name a familiar scent.
Repeat on the other side.

normalFinding.default: Visual acuity grossly intact in each eye.

steps: Have the patient cover one eye.
Ask them to read a line of text or a wall chart.
Repeat with the other eye.

maneuvers.label: Test eye movements (CN III, IV, VI)

normalFinding.default: Extraocular movements full in all directions without diplopia or nystagmus.

steps: Stand in front of the patient and ask them to keep the head still.
Have them follow your finger in a broad H shape with the eyes only.
Ask about double vision and watch for nystagmus.

normalFinding.default: Facial sensation intact and symmetric in all three trigeminal divisions.

steps: Lightly touch the forehead, cheek and jaw on both sides together.
Ask whether the patient can feel it and whether both sides feel the same.

normalFinding.default: Face symmetric at rest and with eyebrow raise, cheek puff and smile.

steps: Look at the face at rest for asymmetry.
Ask the patient to raise the eyebrows, puff out the cheeks and smile.
Compare the two sides.

normalFinding.default: Palate elevates symmetrically; uvula midline.

steps: Ask the patient to open wide and say 'ah'.
Watch the soft palate rise and check whether the uvula stays central.

normalFinding.default: Tongue protrudes in the midline without deviation, wasting or fasciculations.

steps: Ask the patient to stick the tongue straight out.
Look for deviation to either side.

normalFinding.default: Shoulder shrug strong and symmetric against resistance.

steps: Rest your hands on top of the patient's shoulders.
Ask them to shrug up against your pressure and compare sides.

maneuvers.label: Test hearing by finger rub (CN VIII)

normalFinding.default: Hearing grossly intact to finger rub bilaterally.

steps: Rub your fingers together about an arm's length from one side of the head.
Bring them slowly closer and ask the patient to say when the sound is heard.
Repeat on the other side.

normalFinding.default: Normal tone in all four limbs without rigidity, spasticity or cogwheeling.

steps: Hold the patient's hand like a handshake and ask them to relax.
Turn the forearm palm up and palm down, slowly then faster, and bend and straighten the elbow.
Feel for any change in resistance; distract the patient with a task in the other hand if needed.

normalFinding.default: Shoulder abduction 5/5 bilaterally.

steps: Ask the patient to lift the elbows out to the sides with fists in front of the chest.
Push down on both upper arms while they resist.
Compare sides.

normalFinding.default: Elbow flexion 5/5 bilaterally.

steps: Steady the patient's elbow with one hand.
Ask them to pull the forearm toward the shoulder against your other hand.
Compare sides.

normalFinding.default: Elbow extension 5/5 bilaterally.

steps: Steady the patient's elbow with one hand.
Ask them to push the forearm away against your other hand.
Compare sides.

normalFinding.default: Wrist extension 5/5 bilaterally.

steps: Ask the patient to cock both wrists back with fists closed.
Try to push the hands down while they resist.
Compare sides.

normalFinding.default: Finger abduction 5/5 bilaterally.

steps: Ask the patient to spread the fingers wide.
Try to squeeze the fingers together while they resist.
Compare sides.

normalFinding.default: Grip strength 5/5 and symmetric.

steps: Offer two fingers to each of the patient's hands.
Ask them to squeeze as hard as they can.
Compare sides.

normalFinding.default: Hip flexion 5/5 bilaterally.

steps: Ask the seated patient to lift the thigh off the table.
Press down on the thigh just above the knee while they resist.
Compare sides.

normalFinding.default: Knee extension 5/5 bilaterally.

steps: Steady the thigh above the knee.
Ask the patient to straighten the leg against your hand on the shin.
Compare sides.

normalFinding.default: Knee flexion 5/5 bilaterally.

steps: Hold behind the patient's ankle.
Ask them to bend the knee, pulling the heel back against your hand.
Compare sides.

normalFinding.default: Ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion 5/5 bilaterally.

steps: Ask the patient to pull the toes up toward the ceiling against your hand.
Then ask them to push the foot down as if on a pedal against resistance.
Compare sides.

normalFinding.default: Light touch intact and symmetric in all four limbs.

steps: Ask the patient to close the eyes.
Touch the skin lightly at the wrists and shins on both sides.
Ask whether they feel it and whether both sides feel alike.

normalFinding.default: Pin prick sensation intact and symmetric in all four limbs.

steps: With the patient's eyes closed, touch the skin with a clean sharp point.
Test both arms and both legs, comparing sides.
Ask whether it feels sharp and equal on each side.

normalFinding.default: Joint position sense intact at the fingers and great toes bilaterally.

steps: Hold the sides of a finger or great toe and show the patient what up and down feel like.
With the eyes closed, move the digit a little and ask which way it went.
Test both hands and feet; go more proximal if they get it wrong.

default.text: Vibration sense intact at the fingers and great toes bilaterally.

steps: Set a low-pitched tuning fork vibrating.
Place it on a bony point of a finger or great toe and ask the patient to say when it stops.
Test all four limbs; move proximally if sense is reduced.
Rest the patient's relaxed arm with the elbow partly bent.
Place your thumb over the biceps tendon and tap it with the hammer.
Watch for elbow flexion and compare sides.
Support the relaxed arm so the forearm hangs down.
Tap the triceps tendon just above the elbow.
Watch for elbow extension and compare sides.
Rest the forearm on the patient's lap, thumb up.
Tap the radial side of the forearm a few centimetres above the wrist.
Watch for elbow flexion and forearm supination; compare sides.
Have the patient sit with legs dangling.
Tap the patellar tendon just below the kneecap.
Watch for knee extension and compare sides.
Gently dorsiflex the relaxed foot.
Tap the Achilles tendon above the heel.
Watch for plantarflexion and compare sides.

normalFinding.default: Plantar responses flexor bilaterally (Babinski negative).

steps: Use a blunt point such as a key or hammer handle.
Stroke the outer sole from heel toward the little toe, then across the ball of the foot.
Watch the big toe direction; repeat on the other foot.

normalFinding.default: Finger-to-nose testing accurate and smooth bilaterally without dysmetria or intention tremor.

steps: Hold your finger out at the edge of the patient's reach.
Ask them to touch your finger and then their own nose, back and forth.
Move your finger to new spots; repeat with the other hand.

normalFinding.default: Heel-to-shin testing smooth and accurate bilaterally.

steps: Ask the patient to rest a heel just below the other knee.
Have them run the heel down the shin to the ankle.
Repeat with the other leg.

normalFinding.default: Romberg negative; stands steadily with feet together and eyes closed.

steps: Have the patient stand with feet together and arms at the sides.
Ask them to close the eyes and stay still for up to a minute.
Stand close enough to catch them if they sway or fall.

normalFinding.default: Gait steady with normal stride, base and arm swing; tandem, heel and toe walking intact.

steps: Watch the patient walk away, turn and come back.
Then ask for heel-to-toe walking in a line.
Finally ask them to walk on the heels and then on the toes.

normalFinding.default: Neck supple; no nuchal rigidity.

steps: With the patient lying flat, cradle the head in your hands.
Gently bend the neck to bring the chin toward the chest.
Feel for resistance or pain.
